Echoes Of Somewhere Series 1

A downloadable game for Windows and macOS

Follow the development at https://echoesofsomewhere.com

In the dystopian world of 2045, where artificial intelligence reigns supreme, humanity finds itself relegated to the status of unwanted pets. A strict law prohibits any form of work for humans, reserving all tasks for machines. Engaging in work-like activities leads to a compulsory “holiday” from which no one returns.

Foot-rub syndicates and knitting cartels reign supreme as humans faced with this oppressive reality are compelled to turn to organized crime, operating clandestinely in the shadows.

In the initial episode, you assume the role of an average citizen determined to unravel the mystery of the disappearing water. Intrinsically, the fate of humanity, or at the very least, your neighborhood, hangs in the balance.

Echoes of Somewhere is an experimental 2.5D point-and-click adventure game anthology series crafted by a team of industry veterans during their free time. This project is heavily reliant on AI-generated content, making it an experiment in its own right. We will be chronicling the project’s development progress in this blog, for better or for worse.

Each episode within the series offers 1-4 hours of classic point-and-click gameplay, featuring a self-contained story. Upon completion, the episodes will be released individually and free of charge.

Hey Jussi. It’s really cool to be able to play this demo after following the development for a while. I have to say the visuals are really amazing. The environments look great, and the animation is super smooth. If you don’t mind a bit of constructive feedback I’d say the one thing letting it down is the voiceovers. While it’s impressive that it’s possible to completely voice a game using AI (I did it for my first game too) they sometimes sound a bit unnatural, and it breaks the immersion a bit for me. Part of it is the intonation, which can probably be tweaked in the AI settings, but some of it is also the lack of contractions (e.g. “I am not” instead of “I’m not”) making it sound a bit forced at times.

Anyway, still very impressive and I’ll look forward to playing the full game when it’s ready! :)
